I will keep things simple and steady this year. I am 66, and I do not want to take on crops that need too much labor, too much risk, or hard-to-learn management. In Quzhou County, the wheat and summer maize rotation fits my land, the local weather, my experience, and the machines I can hire. I already know how to manage these two crops, the inputs are easy to buy, and I can sell them without much trouble. So I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize cycle instead of trying vegetables, cotton, or other cash crops.

For my winter wheat, I will manage the crop that is already in the field through spring and early summer with stable fertilizer, a few irrigations, and only necessary pesticide sprays. After harvest, I will quickly sow summer maize on the same land so I do not lose moisture or time. I will use improved or hybrid seed, moderate fertilizer, and enough water to protect yield, but I will not overinvest because I care more about a reliable harvest than chasing the highest output. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage because it is familiar, practical, and easier for me to manage than deep ploughing every season or strict no-tillage.
